what: Carnival is the largest cruise company in the world, with nine brands including Carnival Cruise Line, Princess, Holland America, Costa and AIDA, and around 90 ships.
customers: Holidaymakers worldwide, from first-time cruisers on Carnival to older luxury passengers on Cunard and Seabourn.
money: drinks, excursions, casinos and retail on board
moat: Ships that cost over a billion dollars and take years to build, with brand positions across price points and a repeat customer base.
risks: Debt of about $26 billion remains from the pandemic shutdown
Fuel prices and port costs move margins
A health scare or incident can stop bookings across the industry
It only recently restored a dividend
opportunities: Revenue grew about 30% a year over three years as cruising recovered
Onboard spending per passenger keeps setting records
Debt reduction is now the main use of cash, which shifts value to shareholders
watch: Net yields per passenger day and the pace of debt repayment.
